extracted.intended_audience: editors and readers of travel literature; scholars preparing or assessing historical travelogues
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and editing a historical travel journal for publication: selecting and presenting original journals, translations, memoirs, letters, maps and illustrations; making editorial choices explicit; and assessing the narrative's merits (accuracy, style, completeness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial completeness / intent
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal "was written without the slightest view to publication... to recall to his own recollection _other_ particulars..." and therefore is "the mere outline of a much more extended and detailed narrative, which it was the author's intention to prepare for the press after his return to England."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the work as potentially incomplete and make allowances accordingly; state the author's original intent and whether the text represents an outline or a finished account so readers understand limits of scope and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and minute detail as a virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor argues that "the very nakedness and simplicity of its descriptions and its minute details of petty circumstances, may... convey a more accurate and distinct conception of the process of an African journey... than a more elaborate and polished narrative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value plain, unpolished description and small particulars as contributors to accuracy and vividness; do not necessarily smooth or over-polish passages that provide factual or observational detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal marks of truth and fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal "bears strong internal marks of truth and fidelity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reliability by internal coherence and concrete factual detail; emphasize and preserve elements that support the narrative's credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and cataloguing of primary/supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication should include the original journal, translated journals (e.g., Isaaco's Arabic-to-English journal), memoirs, official instructions, letters to authorities, and private letters—enumerated as the principal documents forming the volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect, enumerate and present primary sources (original journals, translations, official papers, private letters) to give readers a full documentary apparatus and authority for the edition; label which items are official vs. private and explain editorial decisions about inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and attribution for private material
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor states that he "is alone responsible for the publication of the private letters, and for whatever else is contained in this volume, besides the official documents."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must explicitly claim responsibility for selection and publication of private materials and disclose editorial judgments about privacy, propriety and provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map construction and reconciliation of observational data
rubrics_metrics.description: In compiling the map "much difficulty has arisen from the bearings of places not being mentioned in the Journal; and... great differences between the latitudes and longitudes of places according to the astronomical observations, and the distances computed according to the journies... considerable pains have been taken to reconcile these differences; but the general result has been, that it was found necessary in adhering to the astronomical observations..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing maps from travel journals, reconcile multiple data sources (astronomical observations, stated bearings, computed distances). Where conflicts exist, document the reconciliation process and (as here) give priority to and justify adherence to astronomical observations; explicitly record mapping assumptions and uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about editorial scope and digressions
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor admits that in preparing the Memoir he "has inadvertently exceeded the limits which he had originally assigned to himself... This circumstance has added considerably to the length of the Memoir and its Appendix; for which, he would willingly believe, that the interest belonging to the topics themselves, will be deemed a sufficient apology."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about scope changes, digressions or expansions in editorial apparatus; apologize or justify deviations from stated scope when appropriate and explain their relevance to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, narrative flow, and stylistic elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Travels were praised for "the clearness of the descriptions, the natural and easy flow of the narration, and the general elegance of the style."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate travel writing on clarity of description, smooth narrative flow, and stylistic quality; preserve passages that demonstrate these strengths and note them in editorial commentary or promotional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational authenticity and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor emphasizes that the "essential merit" of the book consists in the "authentic and important information which it contains" and characterizes it as a great contribution to geographical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize and highlight factual discoveries, novel information and the work's contribution to knowledge when assessing and presenting exploratory travel literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and reproduction of illustrative material
rubrics_metrics.description: The original journal contains "several of Mr. Park's drawings and sketches, illustrative of particular descriptions, which are copied in this publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and reproduce original illustrations, drawings or sketches from the author when they illuminate textual descriptions; identify and credit such materials and indicate when they are faithful copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance transparency and disclosure of gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor discloses that Park's manuscript materials included "short notes or memoranda, written on separate pieces of paper... Where these were wanting, he supplied the deficiency from his memory" and that some loose papers were mislaid or destroyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose provenance of the text, note where content was reconstructed from memory or where original documents are missing, and warn readers about potential consequences for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment and citation of contributors and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor expresses indebtedness to family members, Major Rennell, Zachary Macaulay, Sir Joseph Banks, and others for information, papers and assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit contributors, correspondents and sources in the editorial apparatus; record important assistance and correspondence that informed the edition to strengthen scholarly apparatus and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of abstracts and summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Abstract of the Travels, drawn up by Mr. Bryan Edwards, is noted as being "written with perspicuity and elegance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose abstracts and summaries with clarity and elegance; use them to convey the essentials of the work accurately and attractively to readers.
